correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-variable antiderivative tests give the three conditional regressions. Stationarity of y and z gives E[x]=E[y^2]=-bE[y], hence E[y(y+b)]=0 and the completed-square circle law. Jensen yields theta in [0,1] and the exact variance parabola. Endpoint rigidity and the two-sided support theorem follow from sign of y(y+b) and invariance of the compact support. The packaged checker verifies every nonstandard polynomial and equilibrium identity exactly.

value.rationale: Case P is singled out by its author as the strongest candidate in the simple-flow family for coexistence of strange attractors and limit cycles. The theorem supplies an attractor-independent statistical constraint across every compact recurrent component: all stationary measures lie on one exact mean–variance parabola and any non-equilibrium component must occupy both sides of the slab defined by the two equilibrium y-levels. At the canonical b=1 normalization this becomes the concrete RMS identity E[(y+1/2)^2]=1/4. These constraints are directly relevant for distinguishing genuine coexisting recurrent components from transients or numerical artifacts and are not an arbitrary parameter slice.
